research.website_note: The results repeatedly identify apollo.io as Apollo’s own official site and company page.

strategy.observation: Apollo’s search experience depends on enriched firmographic and intent data, and it shows auto-scores by default when users search for people or companies.
strategy.offer_link: A data enrichment quality audit would test whether the records and fields feeding Apollo’s filters and auto-scores are accurate, complete, and current, which matters because those outputs shape how users search, prioritize, and export prospects inside the product.
hypotheses: The Head of Data may be accountable for keeping Apollo’s people/company data quality high across sources.
Apollo may want to spot stale, duplicated, or inconsistently enriched records before they affect search results or downstream CRM syncs.
The team may be evaluating whether scoring and enrichment inputs behave consistently across segments and geographies.
strategy.angle: When Apollo shows auto-scores and intent/firmographic filters in search, the underlying enrichment quality has to stay clean or the output becomes untrustworthy.
strategy.fit_reason: Apollo’s core product is built on people/company data and scoring, so an external audit of enrichment quality is directly relevant to the data layer that powers search, prioritization, and downstream sales workflows.

draft.subject: Search data quality
draft.body:
I help teams audit enrichment quality in sales databases.

At Apollo, search depends on enriched firmographic and intent data, and auto-scores show up by default. If the records behind those fields drift, search results and prioritization can get noisy fast.

A quality audit checks whether the key people and company fields feeding filters and scores are accurate, complete, and current.

Are you already sampling those records for stale or inconsistent enrichment, or should I send a simple audit outline?
